Individual-level variations in malaria susceptibility and acquisition of clinical protection

Data overview and statistical analysis

Mario Recker

December 2020

Load libraries and relevant data

library(tidyverse)
library(rstanarm)
library(viridis)
library(ggsci)
library(patchwork)
library(ggpmisc)
library(bayesplot)
library(arsenal)

DF = read.csv('spatioTemporalEpisodeHistories.csv')

Data overview

The data contains information about individual clinical malaria episode history of 544 children aged 1-12 years enrolled in the Junju birth cohort. The data is structured as follows:

Variable Type Description
Participant.ID categorical a child’s unique identifier
Year numerical year of sampling
Age numerical age in years
BirthYear numerical a child’s year of birth
BirthQuarter categorical birth quarter, Q1: Jan-Mar, Q2: Apr-Jun, Q3: Jul-Sep, Q4: Oct-Dec
Genotype categorical sickle cell trait (AA: normal, AS: heterozygous sickle cell carrier)
PI numerical prevalence index, summary statistic of clinical malaria incidence in the surrounding area
GotEpisode categorical incidence of clinical episode this year (yes / no)
Episodes numerical number of episodes this year
PrevEpisodes numerical total number of episodes before this year
CumEpisodes numerical total number of episodes, including this year

Overview of Junju epidemiology

Incidence over time

fig1a = DF %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(NEpisodes = sum(Episodes),
            NIndividuals = length(unique(Participant.ID)),
            NGotInfected = length(which(GotEpisode=='yes'))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = NEpisodes)) +
  geom_line(size=1,aes(color='Total number of episodes')) +
  geom_line(aes(y=600*NGotInfected/NIndividuals,color='Proportion with episode'),size=1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis=sec_axis(~ . / 600, name='Proportion of individuals with episodes')) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(DF$Year), max(DF$Year), by = 2)) +
  labs(y='Total number of episodes',
       color = '',
       tag = 'A') +
  theme(legend.position = 'top') +
  scale_color_jco()

fig1b = DF %>%
  filter(GotEpisode == 'yes') %>%
  unique() %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  mutate(EpiCat = ifelse(Episodes==1,'1',ifelse(Episodes>2,'3+','2'))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Year, y=Episodes, fill=EpiCat)) +
  geom_bar(position="stack", stat="identity", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(direction=1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(DF$Year), max(DF$Year), by = 1)) +
  theme(legend.position = 'top') + 
  labs(y = 'Total number of episodes',
       fill = '# episodes',
       tag = 'B')

fig1a / fig1b

Individual infection histories, stratified by birth year

Use all children for a select number of birth years and highlight those with the sickle cell trait (heterozygote, AS)

rects = data.frame(start=c(2013,2017), end=c(2014,2018), group=c(1,2))

DF %>%
  filter(BirthYear %in% 2007:2012) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0('Birth year = ',BirthYear)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = CumEpisodes, group = Participant.ID, col = Genotype)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~BirthYear, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(2007,2018,by=2)) +
  scale_color_aaas() +
  geom_rect(data=rects, inherit.aes=FALSE, aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=0, ymax=max(DF$CumEpisodes),
                                               group=group), color="transparent", fill="orange", alpha=0.1) +
  labs(y='Cumulative episodes')

Effect of age and previous episodes on risk of clinical malaria

Note, AS children are filtered for the second graph (not the first one, though) because of its known protective effect, which affects theboth the previous number of episodes and probability of an episode in a given year.

fa = DF %>%
  group_by(GotEpisode) %>%
  mutate(n = n()) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(GotEpisode,'\n(N = ',n,')')) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = Age, fill=GotEpisode)) +
  geom_violin(width = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, col='white', fill='black') +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(2,15,by=2)) +
  theme(legend.position = '') +
  labs(x = 'Clinical episode',
       y = 'Age [years]',
       tag = 'A') +
  scale_fill_jco()

fb = DF %>%
  filter(Genotype=='AA') %>%
  group_by(GotEpisode) %>%
  mutate(n = n()) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(GotEpisode,'\n(N = ',n,')')) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = PrevEpisodes, fill=GotEpisode)) +
  geom_violin(width = 0.9) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, col='white', fill='black') +
  theme(legend.position = '') +
  labs(x = 'Clinical episode',
       y = 'Previous epsisodes',
       tag = 'B') +
  scale_fill_jco() 


fa + fb

Effect of previous episodes, stratified by age

DF %>%
  filter(Genotype=='AA') %>%
  mutate(label = paste(Age,'years',sep=' ')) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = paste(1:12,'years',sep=' '))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = GotEpisode, y = PrevEpisodes/Age, fill=GotEpisode)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(height=0,width=0.05, size=0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~label) +
  theme(legend.position = '') +
  labs(x = 'Clinical episode',
       y = 'Previous number of epsisodes') +
  scale_fill_jco()

Effect of birth quarter on total number of clinical episodes

For this analysis we only take a single reading from each child at a given age (here: 6 years) as the number of episdoes should be directlty linked to age. Because AS is not assumed to make a difference, these are kept in.

##### calculate risk ratio ####
datalist = list()
for(i in 1:6){
  age = i*2
  IDs = which(DF$Age>(i-1)*2 & DF$Age<=i*2)
  Na = length(which(DF$BirthQuarter[IDs]=='Q4'))
  a = length(which(DF$BirthQuarter[IDs]=='Q4' & DF$GotEpisode[IDs]=='yes'))
  Nb = length(IDs)-Na
  b = length(which(DF$BirthQuarter[IDs]!='Q4' & DF$GotEpisode[IDs]=='yes'))
  dat = matrix(c(Nb-b,b,Na-a,a),2,2,byrow=TRUE)
  risk = epitools::riskratio(dat,conf.level=0.95)
  datalist[[age]] = data.frame(Age = paste0(1+2*(i-1),'-',2*i),
                               N = paste0(1+2*(i-1),'-',2*i,'\n(N=',length(IDs),')'),
                               RR = risk$measure[2,1],
                               RR_CI_low = risk$measure[2,2],
                               RR_CI_high = risk$measure[2,3])
}

fa = DF %>%
  filter(Age == 6) %>%
  group_by(BirthQuarter) %>% 
  mutate(n = n()) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(BirthQuarter,'\n(n=',n,')')) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = CumEpisodes, group = BirthQuarter, fill = factor(BirthQuarter))) +
  geom_boxplot(width=0.5,alpha=0.75, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.05, height = 0, size=0.7) +
  scale_fill_d3() +
  labs(x = 'Birth quarter',
       y = 'Cumulative episodes',
       tag = 'A') +
  theme(legend.position = '')



fb = do.call(rbind,datalist) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = RR)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype=2, size=0.25, col='darkblue') +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=RR_CI_low,ymax=RR_CI_high), width=0.2) +
  geom_point(col='red') +
  labs(y = 'Risk ratio (Q4)',
       x = 'Age group [years]',
       tag = 'B')

fa / fb

Statistical modelling

All analyses are done in a Bayesian framework, using rstanarm or brms (both are different front ends that run stan under hood; rstanarm is definitely faster but brms does come with other functionality for plotting the results, like conditional effect plost).

Create data frame for downstream analysis

To facilitate comparison between effects of different covariates (and help with convergence) we centre and scale all numerical variables. Note, we revert back to the original data frame for the conditional effect plots to display re-scaled parameter ranges.

XY = DF %>% 
  mutate(EpiRate = PrevEpisodes/(1+Age), 
         BirthYear = as.factor(BirthYear),
         Year = as.factor(Year)) %>%
  mutate(PI = scale(PI, center = T, scale = T),
         EpiRate = scale(EpiRate, center = T, scale = T),
         PrevEpisodes = scale(PrevEpisodes, center = T, scale = T),
         Age = scale(Age, center = T, scale = T))

YY = XY %>%
  filter(Genotype=='AA')

Model (I)

For this model we consider the following covariates: PI, Age, Genotype and BirthQuarter. That is, we include sickle cell carriers in order to have a direct comparison (of effect sizes) between this and other protective effects.

  1. run model
fullMod = stan_glmer(GotEpisode ~ PI + Genotype  + BirthQuarter + Age + (1|Participant.ID),
                     family = binomial, data = XY, chains = 4, cores = 4)
  1. plot
bayesplot_theme_set(theme_default(base_size = 12, base_family = "sans"))

plot(fullMod, "intervals", pars=c('PI','Age'), regex_pars=c("Birth","Genotype"), prob=0.8, prob_outer=0.95) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype='dotted', col='red', size=0.3) +
  labs(x = 'estimate')

check ‘random’ effect, i.e. distribution of intercepts

u0 = ranef(fullMod)$Participant.ID
raneffect = data.frame(Participant.ID = row.names(u0),
                       Intercept = u0[,1])

ggplot(raneffect, aes(x=Intercept)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y=..density..), color="black", fill="white", bins=15) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=median(Intercept)),
             color="blue", linetype="dashed", size=1) +
  geom_density(alpha=.2, fill="#66FF66")

model comparison with non-hierarchical model using ELDP

  1. run model
nullMod = stan_glm(GotEpisode ~ PI + Genotype  + BirthQuarter + Age,
                   family = binomial, data = XY, chains = 4, cores = 4)
  1. compare using loo’s ELPD
loo_null = loo(nullMod)
loo_full = loo(fullMod)
print(list(loo_null, loo_full, loo_compare(loo_null,loo_full)))

Conditional effect plots

  1. run model
brmMod = brms::brm(GotEpisode ~ PI + BirthQuarter + Age + Genotype + (1|Participant.ID), 
                   family = 'categorical', data = DF, cores=4)
  1. plot
plots = brms::conditional_effects(brmMod, categorical=T)

fa = plot(plots, plot=F)[[1]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco()

fb = plot(plots, plot=F)[[4]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco()

fc = plot(plots, plot=F)[[2]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco()

fd = plot(plots, plot=F)[[3]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,12,by=2)) 


(fa + fb) / (fc + fd)

Model (II)

Instead of using birth quarter or genotype, here we investigate the effect of previous episodes on the probability of a clinical episode. As before we use both rstanarm and brms to create posterior and conditional effect plots (brms can also be used to produce posterior plots but creates weird variable names).

  1. run model
altMod = stan_glmer(GotEpisode ~ PI + PrevEpisodes*Age + (1|Participant.ID),
                     family = binomial, data = YY, chains = 4, cores = 4)
  1. plot
plot(altMod, "intervals", pars=c('PI','Age'), regex_pars=c('Prev'), parprob=0.8,
             prob_outer=0.95) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype='dotted', col='red', size=0.3) +
  labs(x = 'estimate')

conditional effect plots

  1. run model
altbrmMod = brms::brm(GotEpisode ~ PI + PrevEpisodes*Age  + (1|Participant.ID), 
                      family = 'categorical', data = DF[DF$Genotype=='AA',], cores=4)
  1. plot
plots = brms::conditional_effects(altbrmMod, categorical=T)

fa = plot(plots, plot=F)[[1]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco() +
  theme(legend.position = 'top')

fb = plot(plots, plot=F)[[2]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco() +
  theme(legend.position = '') +
  labs(x = 'Previous episodes')

fc = plot(plots, plot=F)[[3]] +
  scale_color_jco() +
  scale_fill_jco() +
  theme(legend.position = '') +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,12,by=2))


fa / fb / fc
